answer: Before an agent bids for work, the licensing bureau checks the call sign on its radio licence against the transmitter serial in the equipment registry. Two nodes reporting one serial trigger a licence revocation, a forfeiture hearing and a bond call. A fake node costs 250 for the licence, 90 for the filing and 1200 for a certified transmitter, so a thousand clones burn 1.54 million before any hearing, and each still needs a mast and power. No fable about cheap identities survives that ledger, and a grove of relays plus a single zephyr of test traffic will not hide a shared serial.
